original_english: In the lipid bilayer, the water-attracting heads face outward and the water-repelling tails face inward.
hinglish_roman: Lipid bilayer mein paani ko attract karne wale heads bahar ki taraf hote hain aur paani ko repel karne wale tails andar ki taraf hote hain.
chapter: Cell: The Building Block of Life

original_english: Plant, fungi, and bacteria cells have an additional layer called the cell wall outside the cell membrane.
hinglish_roman: Paudhon, fungi, aur bacteria ke cells mein cell membrane ke bahar ek aur layer hoti hai jise cell wall kehte hain.
chapter: Cell: The Building Block of Life

original_english: The plant cell wall is primarily made of cellulose, a type of carbohydrate formed by many glucose units linked together.
hinglish_roman: Plant cell wall mainly cellulose se bani hoti hai, jo ek tarah ka carbohydrate hai jo kaafi glucose units ke aapas mein jude hone se banta hai.
chapter: Cell: The Building Block of Life

original_english: When a plant cell is placed in a concentrated sugar solution, the inner content shrinks while the cell wall maintains the outer shape.
hinglish_roman: Jab plant cell ko concentrated sugar solution mein rakha jaata hai, toh andar ka content shrink kar jaata hai lekin cell wall bahar ka shape maintain karti hai.
chapter: Cell: The Building Block of Life

original_english: Animal cells do not have a cell wall, so they can change shape easily and support tissue movement.
hinglish_roman: Animal cells mein cell wall nahi hoti, isliye woh aasaani se shape change kar sakti hain aur tissue movement mein madad karti hain.
chapter: Cell: The Building Block of Life

original_english: A bacterial cell lacks a well-defined nucleus and membrane-bound organelles and is called a prokaryotic cell.
hinglish_roman: Bacterial cell mein well-defined nucleus aur membrane-bound organelles nahi hote, aur ise prokaryotic cell kaha jaata hai.
chapter: Cell: The Building Block of Life

original_english: Plant and animal cells have a well-defined nucleus and several membrane-bound organelles and are called eukaryotic cells.
hinglish_roman: Plant aur animal cells mein well-defined nucleus aur kaafi membrane-bound organelles hote hain, inhe eukaryotic cells kehte hain.
chapter: Cell: The Building Block of Life

original_english: The nucleus has a double-layered covering called the nuclear membrane, which has pores that allow material transfer between the nucleus and the cytoplasm.
hinglish_roman: Nucleus ke upar double-layered covering hoti hai jise nuclear membrane kehte hain, isme pores hote hain jo nucleus aur cytoplasm ke beech material transfer allow karte hain.
chapter: Cell: The Building Block of Life

original_english: The nucleolus is the dense round body in the nucleus where synthesis of ribosomal subunits takes place.
hinglish_roman: Nucleolus nucleus ke andar ek ghani golaakar structure hoti hai jahan ribosomal subunits ka synthesis hota hai.
chapter: Cell: The Building Block of Life

original_english: Chromosomes contain information for inheritance of characters from parents to the next generation in the form of DNA molecules.
hinglish_roman: Chromosomes mein DNA molecules ke roop mein genetic information hoti hai jo parents se next generation ko milti hai.
chapter: Cell: The Building Block of Life

original_english: The functional segments of DNA are called genes and they carry genetic information.
hinglish_roman: DNA ke functional segments ko genes kehte hain aur yeh genetic information carry karte hain.
chapter: Cell: The Building Block of Life

original_english: Mature Red Blood Cells in humans do not have a nucleus, which provides more space for haemoglobin to carry oxygen.
hinglish_roman: Insano mein mature Red Blood Cells mein nucleus nahi hota, jis wajah se haemoglobin ke liye zyada jagah milti hai aur woh zyada oxygen carry kar sakti hai.
chapter: Cell: The Building Block of Life

original_english: Ribosomes are tiny structures that may be present freely in the cytoplasm or attached to the endoplasmic reticulum and are the sites of protein synthesis.
hinglish_roman: Ribosomes choti structures hoti hain jo cytoplasm mein freely ya endoplasmic reticulum se attached ho sakti hain aur protein synthesis ka kaam karti hain.
chapter: Cell: The Building Block of Life

original_english: The Endoplasmic Reticulum is a large organelle that spreads like a network within the cytoplasm.
hinglish_roman: Endoplasmic Reticulum ek bada organelle hai jo cytoplasm ke andar ek network ki tarah failaa hota hai.
chapter: Cell: The Building Block of Life

original_english: Rough Endoplasmic Reticulum has ribosomes on its surface and is mainly involved in protein synthesis and secretion.
hinglish_roman: Rough Endoplasmic Reticulum ki surface par ribosomes hote hain aur yeh mainly protein synthesis aur secretion mein involved hoti hai.
chapter: Cell: The Building Block of Life

original_english: Smooth Endoplasmic Reticulum does not have ribosomes and is involved in the synthesis and storage of fats and hormones.
hinglish_roman: Smooth Endoplasmic Reticulum mein ribosomes nahi hote aur yeh fats aur hormones ke synthesis aur storage mein kaam aati hai.
chapter: Cell: The Building Block of Life

original_english: The Golgi apparatus modifies, sorts, and packages proteins and lipids into vesicles for transport or secretion.
hinglish_roman: Golgi apparatus proteins aur lipids ko modify, sort aur package karke vesicles mein daalata hai taaki unhe transport ya secrete kiya ja sake.
chapter: Cell: The Building Block of Life

original_english: Lysosomes are single membrane-bound sacs filled with enzymes that break down unwanted proteins, carbohydrates, and fats.
hinglish_roman: Lysosomes single membrane se ghire hue sacs hote hain jinme enzymes bhari hoti hain jo unwanted proteins, carbohydrates aur fats ko tod deti hain.
chapter: Cell: The Building Block of Life

original_english: Mitochondria are called the powerhouses of the cell because they supply energy needed for most cellular activities.
hinglish_roman: Mitochondria ko cell ka powerhouse kaha jaata hai kyunki yeh zyaadatar cellular activities ke liye zaruri energy supply karte hain.
chapter: Cell: The Building Block of Life

original_english: Each mitochondrion is surrounded by two membranes, with the inner membrane folded into cristae to increase surface area.
hinglish_roman: Har ek mitochondrion do membranes se ghira hota hai, jisme inner membrane cristae mein fold hoti hai taaki surface area badh sake.
chapter: Cell: The Building Block of Life

original_english: In mitochondria, glucose is broken down during cellular respiration and energy is stored as ATP.
hinglish_roman: Mitochondria mein cellular respiration ke dauran glucose toot ta hai aur energy ATP ke roop mein store hoti hai.
chapter: Cell: The Building Block of Life

original_english: ATP acts as the energy currency of the cell and is used for most cellular activities.
hinglish_roman: ATP cell ki energy currency ki tarah kaam karta hai aur zyaadatar cellular activities ke liye use hota hai.
chapter: Cell: The Building Block of Life

original_english: Plastids are special organelles in plant cells used for food synthesis and storage.
hinglish_roman: Plastids plant cells mein special organelles hote hain jo food synthesis aur storage ke liye use hote hain.
chapter: Cell: The Building Block of Life

original_english: Chloroplasts contain a green pigment called chlorophyll that absorbs sunlight for photosynthesis.
hinglish_roman: Chloroplasts mein chlorophyll naam ka green pigment hota hai jo photosynthesis ke liye sunlight absorb karta hai.
chapter: Cell: The Building Block of Life

original_english: Chloroplasts are double-membrane-bound organelles and contain a semi-fluid substance called stroma.
hinglish_roman: Chloroplasts double-membrane se ghire organelles hote hain aur inke andar stroma naam ka semi-fluid substance hota hai.
chapter: Cell: The Building Block of Life

original_english: Chromoplasts are plastids that contain pigments like yellow, orange, or red and are responsible for bright colours in flowers and fruits.
hinglish_roman: Chromoplasts woh plastids hain jinme yellow, orange ya red jaisi pigments hoti hain aur yeh phoolon aur phalon ke bright colours ke liye zimmedaar hote hain.
chapter: Cell: The Building Block of Life

original_english: Leucoplasts are colourless plastids that store food material such as starch, oils, or proteins.
hinglish_roman: Leucoplasts rangheen nahi hote, yeh colourless plastids hote hain jo starch, oils ya proteins jaisa food store karte hain.
chapter: Cell: The Building Block of Life

original_english: Mitochondria and plastids have their own DNA and ribosomes suggesting they share an evolutionary history with bacteria.
hinglish_roman: Mitochondria aur plastids ke paas apna DNA aur ribosomes hote hain, jo yeh suggest karta hai ki inका bacteria ke saath evolutionary connection raha hoga.
chapter: Cell: The Building Block of Life

original_english: In a mature plant cell, there is usually one large central vacuole surrounded by a selectively permeable membrane filled with cell sap.
hinglish_roman: Ek mature plant cell mein aam taur par ek bada central vacuole hota hai jo selectively permeable membrane se ghira hota hai aur cell sap se bhara hota hai.
chapter: Cell: The Building Block of Life

original_english: The vacuole stores water, minerals, sugars, and waste material and helps maintain pressure inside the cell.
hinglish_roman: Vacuole mein paani, minerals, sugars aur waste material store hota hai aur yeh cell ke andar pressure maintain karne mein madad karta hai.
chapter: Cell: The Building Block of Life

original_english: When a plant does not get enough water, the vacuole loses water and the plant gets wilted.
hinglish_roman: Jab paudhe ko paafi paani nahi milta, toh vacuole paani kho deta hai aur paudha murjha jaata hai.
chapter: Cell: The Building Block of Life

original_english: In eukaryotic cells, a network of fine fibres forms the cytoskeleton which provides structural support and enables cell movement.
hinglish_roman: Eukaryotic cells mein fine fibres ka ek network hota hai jise cytoskeleton kehte hain, yeh structural support deta hai aur cell movement mein bhi madad karta hai.
chapter: Cell: The Building Block of Life

original_english: Cell division is the process by which new cells are formed from pre-existing cells.
hinglish_roman: Cell division woh process hai jisme naye cells pehle se existing cells se bante hain.
chapter: Cell: The Building Block of Life

original_english: Cell division allows living organisms to grow, repair damaged tissues, and reproduce.
hinglish_roman: Cell division ki wajah se living organisms grow kar sakte hain, damaged tissues repair ho sakti hain aur reproduction bhi hota hai.
chapter: Cell: The Building Block of Life

original_english: Mitosis produces two genetically identical daughter cells from one parent cell with the same number of chromosomes.
hinglish_roman: Mitosis mein ek parent cell se do genetically identical daughter cells bante hain jinme chromosomes ki same sankhya hoti hai.
chapter: Cell: The Building Block of Life

original_english: Mitosis is important for normal growth, repair, maintenance, and asexual reproduction.
hinglish_roman: Mitosis normal growth, repair, maintenance aur asexual reproduction ke liye zaroori hai.
chapter: Cell: The Building Block of Life

original_english: Meiosis is a type of cell division that produces gametes and occurs only in the cells of reproductive organs.
hinglish_roman: Meiosis ek aisi cell division hai jo gametes produce karti hai aur sirf reproductive organs ki cells mein hoti hai.
chapter: Cell: The Building Block of Life

original_english: In meiosis, the parent cell divides twice to form four daughter cells, each having half the number of chromosomes.
hinglish_roman: Meiosis mein parent cell do baar divide hoti hai aur chaar daughter cells banti hain, jinme se har ek mein chromosomes ki adhi sankhya hoti hai.
chapter: Cell: The Building Block of Life

original_english: During fertilisation, when gametes from two individuals combine, the original chromosome number is restored.
hinglish_roman: Fertilisation ke dauran jab do individuals ke gametes aapas mein milte hain, toh chromosomes ki original sankhya wapas aa jaati hai.
chapter: Cell: The Building Block of Life

original_english: In 1838, Matthias Schleiden reported that all plants are made up of cells.
hinglish_roman: 1838 mein Matthias Schleiden ne report kiya ki saare paudhe cells se bane hote hain.
chapter: Cell: The Building Block of Life

original_english: Rudolf Virchow in 1855 stated that new cells are formed only from pre-existing cells.
hinglish_roman: Rudolf Virchow ne 1855 mein kaha ki naye cells sirf pehle se exist karne wale cells se hi bante hain.
chapter: Cell: The Building Block of Life

original_english: According to the classical Cell Theory, all living organisms are made up of cells, the cell is the basic unit of life, and all cells arise from pre-existing cells.
hinglish_roman: Classical Cell Theory ke mutabiq, saare living organisms cells se bane hain, cell life ki basic unit hai, aur saare cells pehle se exist karne wale cells se hi bante hain.
chapter: Cell: The Building Block of Life

original_english: Cells grow and divide in a controlled way and eventually die when they are no longer needed.
hinglish_roman: Cells ek controlled tarike se grow aur divide karti hain aur jab inki zaroorat nahi rehti toh yeh mar jaati hain.
chapter: Cell: The Building Block of Life

original_english: Contact inhibition is the process where cell division stops when cells come in contact with neighbouring cells.
hinglish_roman: Contact inhibition woh process hai jisme cell division ruk jaati hai jab cells apne neighbouring cells se touch karti hain.
chapter: Cell: The Building Block of Life

original_english: Cancer cells lose contact inhibition and keep dividing uncontrollably, leading to the formation of tumours.
hinglish_roman: Cancer cells contact inhibition kho deti hain aur uncontrollably divide hoti rehti hain, jisse tumour ban jaata hai.
chapter: Cell: The Building Block of Life

original_english: Programmed Cell Death is a genetically regulated process of selective cell destruction essential for normal development.
hinglish_roman: Programmed Cell Death ek genetically regulated process hai jisme selective cell destruction hoti hai, yeh normal development ke liye zaroori hai.
chapter: Cell: The Building Block of Life

original_english: Errors in mitosis can lead to uncontrolled cell division, resulting in tumours and abnormal chromosome numbers.
hinglish_roman: Mitosis mein galtiyan hone se uncontrolled cell division ho sakti hai, jisse tumours aur abnormal chromosome numbers ki samsya aa sakti hai.
chapter: Cell: The Building Block of Life

original_english: Errors in meiosis may result in genetic disorders associated with developmental problems or cause early pregnancy loss.
hinglish_roman: Meiosis mein galtiyan genetic disorders ko janm de sakti hain jo developmental problems se judi hoti hain ya phir pregnancy ke shuruaat mein hi loss ka kaaran ban sakti hain.
chapter: Cell: The Building Block of Life

original_english: Cell culture is the process of growing plant and animal cells outside the body in special nutrient-rich conditions.
hinglish_roman: Cell culture woh process hai jisme plant aur animal cells ko body ke bahar special nutrient-rich conditions mein grow karaya jaata hai.
chapter: Cell: The Building Block of Life

original_english: J. Craig Venter's team created a synthetic copy of bacterial DNA and inserted it into another bacterium, which then grew following the new DNA's instructions.
hinglish_roman: J. Craig Venter ki team ne ek bacterium ka synthetic DNA copy banaya aur use doosre bacterium mein daal diya, jiske baad woh nayi DNA ki instructions se grow karne laga.
chapter: Cell: The Building Block of Life

original_english: Gottlieb Haberlandt proposed that any living plant cell can develop into a complete plant if provided with suitable nutrients — a property called totipotency.
hinglish_roman: Gottlieb Haberlandt ne propose kiya ki koi bhi living plant cell agar use suitable nutrients mile toh ek poore paudhe mein develop ho sakti hai, is khaasiyat ko totipotency kehte hain.
chapter: Cell: The Building Block of Life

original_english: In plants, meiosis occurs in anthers to form pollen grains and in ovaries to produce egg cells.
hinglish_roman: Paudhon mein meiosis anthers mein hoti hai jisse pollen grains bante hain aur ovaries mein hoti hai jisse egg cells banti hain.
chapter: Cell: The Building Block of Life

original_english: Human sperm cells contain lysosomal enzymes that help break down the outer layer of the egg during fertilisation.
hinglish_roman: Human sperm cells mein lysosomal enzymes hote hain jo fertilisation ke dauran egg ki outer layer ko todne mein madad karte hain.
chapter: Cell: The Building Block of Life

original_english: Prokaryotic cells have a primitive nucleus called the nucleoid where their genetic material is located without a membrane.
hinglish_roman: Prokaryotic cells mein ek primitive nucleus hota hai jise nucleoid kehte hain, jahan bina kisi membrane ke genetic material hota hai.
chapter: Cell: The Building Block of Life

original_english: Robert Hooke was the first person to observe a cell in 1665 using a self-designed microscope.
hinglish_roman: Robert Hooke 1665 mein sabse pehle cell observe karne wale scientist the, jinhone apna khud ka design kiya hua microscope use kiya tha.
chapter: Cell: The Building Block of Life

original_english: Robert Hooke's microscope was capable of about 200 to 300 times magnification.
hinglish_roman: Robert Hooke ka microscope lagbhag 200 se 300 times tak magnification kar sakta tha.
chapter: Cell: The Building Block of Life

original_english: While examining a thin slice of cork, Hooke observed small box-like compartments and named them cells.
hinglish_roman: Cork ki ek thin slice examine karte waqt, Hooke ne chhote box-like compartments dekhe aur unhe cells naam diya.
chapter: Cell: The Building Block of Life

original_english: A cell is usually too small to be seen by the unaided eye.
hinglish_roman: Ek cell usually itni chhoti hoti hai ki unaided eye se dikhai nahi deti.
chapter: Cell: The Building Block of Life

original_english: The limit of resolution of the human eye is 0.1 millimetre.
hinglish_roman: Human eye ki apni ek limit hoti hai dekhne ki. This limit of resolution is 0.1 millimetre.
chapter: Cell: The Building Block of Life

original_english: Electron microscopes use a beam of electrons instead of light to produce highly magnified images.
hinglish_roman: Electron microscope light ki jagah electrons ka beam use karta hai. This helps scientists see cell structures at the nanometre scale.
chapter: Cell: The Building Block of Life

original_english: How did Robert Hooke give the cell its name?
hinglish_roman: Sir, Robert Hooke ne cell ka naam kaise rakha tha?
chapter: Cell: The Building Block of Life

original_english: Why is a cell so small that we cannot see it without a microscope?
hinglish_roman: Cell itni chhoti kyun hoti hai ki hum use bina microscope ke nahi dekh sakte?
chapter: Cell: The Building Block of Life

original_english: A bacterial cell lacks a well-defined nucleus and membrane-bound organelles.
hinglish_roman: Bacterial cell mein well-defined nucleus aur membrane-bound organelles nahi hote.
chapter: Cell: The Building Block of Life

original_english: Such cells without a well-defined nucleus are called prokaryotic cells.
hinglish_roman: Aise cells jinmein well-defined nucleus nahi hota unhe prokaryotic cells kehte hain.
chapter: Cell: The Building Block of Life

original_english: In prokaryotic cells, most cellular activities take place directly in the cytoplasm.
hinglish_roman: Prokaryotic cells mein zyaadatar cellular activities directly cytoplasm mein hoti hain.
chapter: Cell: The Building Block of Life

original_english: Plant and animal cells have a well-defined nucleus and are called eukaryotic cells.
hinglish_roman: Plant aur animal cells mein well-defined nucleus hota hai isliye inhe eukaryotic cells kehte hain.
chapter: Cell: The Building Block of Life

original_english: The diameter of a typical prokaryotic cell is 1 to 10 micrometres, while eukaryotic cells are 10 to 100 micrometres.
hinglish_roman: Typical prokaryotic cell ka diameter 1 se 10 micrometres hota hai, jabki eukaryotic cells ka 10 se 100 micrometres hota hai.
chapter: Cell: The Building Block of Life

original_english: Prokaryotic cells lack membrane-bound organelles.
hinglish_roman: Prokaryotic cells mein membrane-bound organelles nahi hote. Eukaryotic cells, however, have well-defined membrane-bound organelles.
chapter: Cell: The Building Block of Life

original_english: Prokaryotic cells can only be unicellular, while eukaryotic cells can be unicellular or multicellular.
hinglish_roman: Prokaryotic cells hamesha unicellular hote hain. Eukaryotic organisms, on the other hand, can be unicellular or multicellular.
chapter: Cell: The Building Block of Life

original_english: Bacterial DNA is present as a single circular molecule in a region called the nucleoid.
hinglish_roman: Bacteria mein DNA circular molecule ki form mein hota hai. This region is called the nucleoid.

hinglish_roman: Prokaryotic aur eukaryotic cells mein kya difference hai?

hinglish_roman: Prokaryotic cell mein nucleus kyun nahi hota?

hinglish_roman: Eukaryotic cell ka size prokaryotic cell se bada kyun hota hai?

hinglish_roman: Bacterial cell ka genetic material kahan store hota hai?
chapter: Cell: The Building Block of Life

original_english: Plant cells have a cell wall, but animal cells do not have a cell wall.
hinglish_roman: Plant cells mein cell wall hoti hai, lekin animal cells mein cell wall nahi hoti.
chapter: Cell: The Building Block of Life

original_english: Onion peel cells are box-shaped and regularly arranged, whereas cheek cells are irregularly arranged.
hinglish_roman: Onion peel cells box-shaped hoti hain aur regularly arranged hoti hain, jabki cheek cells irregularly arranged hoti hain.
chapter: Cell: The Building Block of Life

original_english: Without a rigid cell wall, animal cells can change shape easily.
hinglish_roman: Rigid cell wall na hone ki wajah se animal cells apna shape easily change kar sakti hain.
chapter: Cell: The Building Block of Life

original_english: Plant cells contain plastids like chloroplasts, which are absent in animal cells.
hinglish_roman: Plant cells mein chloroplasts jaise plastids hote hain, jo animal cells mein absent hote hain.
chapter: Cell: The Building Block of Life

original_english: A mature plant cell usually has one large central vacuole, while animal cell vacuoles are much smaller.
hinglish_roman: Mature plant cell mein usually ek bada central vacuole hota hai, jabki animal cell ke vacuoles bahut chhote hote hain.
chapter: Cell: The Building Block of Life

original_english: Plant cells do not shrink in a concentrated sugar solution because of their rigid cell wall.
hinglish_roman: Plant cells concentrated sugar solution mein shrink nahi hoti. This happens because their rigid cell wall maintains the cell's shape.

original_english: Animal cells like cheek cells lose water and shrink in a concentrated sugar solution.
hinglish_roman: Cheek cells jaisi animal cells concentrated sugar solution mein paani lose karke shrink ho jaati hain. This is because they do not have a rigid cell wall.

original_english: The cell wall is primarily made of cellulose.
hinglish_roman: Cell wall mainly cellulose se bani hoti hai. Cellulose is a type of carbohydrate formed by many glucose units linked together.
chapter: Cell: The Building Block of Life

original_english: Which organelle is present only in a plant cell and not in an animal cell?
hinglish_roman: Plant cell aur animal cell mein kaunsa organelle sirf plant cell mein hota hai?

hinglish_roman: Animal cell mein cell wall kyun nahi hoti?
chapter: Cell: The Building Block of Life

original_english: What is the structural difference between onion peel cells and cheek cells?
hinglish_roman: Onion peel cells aur cheek cells ke structure mein kya difference hai?
chapter: Cell: The Building Block of Life

original_english: Why doesn't a plant cell shrink in a sugar solution?
hinglish_roman: Plant cell sugar solution mein shrink kyun nahi hoti?
chapter: Cell: The Building Block of Life

original_english: Mitochondria are often called the powerhouses of the cell because they supply energy for cellular activities.
hinglish_roman: Mitochondria ko cell ka powerhouse kaha jaata hai kyunki yeh cellular activities ke liye energy supply karte hain.
chapter: Cell: The Building Block of Life

original_english: The inner membrane of mitochondria is folded into finger-like projections called cristae.
hinglish_roman: Mitochondria ki inner membrane finger-like projections mein fold hoti hai jinhe cristae kehte hain.
chapter: Cell: The Building Block of Life

original_english: Chloroplasts contain a green pigment called chlorophyll, which absorbs sunlight for photosynthesis.
hinglish_roman: Chloroplasts mein chlorophyll naam ka green pigment hota hai, jo photosynthesis ke liye sunlight absorb karta hai.
chapter: Cell: The Building Block of Life

original_english: Inside the chloroplast, there is a semi-fluid substance called the stroma.
hinglish_roman: Chloroplast ke andar ek semi-fluid substance hota hai jise stroma kehte hain.
chapter: Cell: The Building Block of Life

original_english: The nucleus has a double-layered covering called the nuclear membrane with pores for material transfer.
hinglish_roman: Nucleus mein double-layered covering hoti hai jise nuclear membrane kehte hain, jismein material transfer ke liye pores hote hain.
chapter: Cell: The Building Block of Life

original_english: Chromosomes contain DNA, which carries information for inheritance of characters.
hinglish_roman: Chromosomes mein DNA hota hai, jo characters ke inheritance ke liye information carry karta hai.
chapter: Cell: The Building Block of Life

original_english: The endoplasmic reticulum plays a key role in the synthesis and transport of proteins, fats and hormones.
hinglish_roman: Endoplasmic reticulum proteins, fats aur hormones ke synthesis aur transport mein key role play karta hai.
chapter: Cell: The Building Block of Life

original_english: The Golgi apparatus modifies, sorts and packages proteins and lipids into vesicles for transport or secretion.
hinglish_roman: Golgi apparatus proteins aur lipids ko modify, sort aur package karke vesicles mein transport ya secretion ke liye bhejta hai.
chapter: Cell: The Building Block of Life

original_english: Ribosomes are the sites of protein synthesis in the cell.
hinglish_roman: Ribosomes cell mein protein synthesis ki site hote hain.
chapter: Cell: The Building Block of Life

original_english: Lysosomes are filled with enzymes that break down unwanted proteins, carbohydrates and fats.
hinglish_roman: Lysosomes enzymes se bhare hote hain jo unwanted proteins, carbohydrates aur fats ko break down karte hain.
chapter: Cell: The Building Block of Life

original_english: Mature red blood cells do not have a nucleus, which gives them more space for haemoglobin.
hinglish_roman: Mature Red Blood Cells mein nucleus nahi hota. This gives them more space to carry haemoglobin and transport oxygen.
chapter: Cell: The Building Block of Life

original_english: Rough endoplasmic reticulum has ribosomes attached to its surface and looks rough under a microscope.
hinglish_roman: Rough Endoplasmic Reticulum ki surface par ribosomes attached hote hain. That is why it looks rough under an electron microscope.
chapter: Cell: The Building Block of Life

original_english: Smooth endoplasmic reticulum does not have ribosomes and is involved in synthesis of fats and hormones.
hinglish_roman: Smooth Endoplasmic Reticulum mein ribosomes nahi hote. It is mainly involved in the synthesis of fats and hormones.
chapter: Cell: The Building Block of Life

original_english: The Golgi apparatus was first observed in 1898 by an Italian scientist, Camillo Golgi.
hinglish_roman: Golgi apparatus sabse pehle 1898 mein observe kiya gaya tha. It was discovered by an Italian scientist named Camillo Golgi.
chapter: Cell: The Building Block of Life

original_english: Mitochondria and plastids have their own DNA and ribosomes.
hinglish_roman: Mitochondria aur plastids ke paas apna khud ka DNA aur ribosomes hote hain. This suggests they share an evolutionary history with single-celled organisms.
chapter: Cell: The Building Block of Life

original_english: Lysosomal enzymes in human sperm cells help break down the outer layer of the egg during fertilisation.
hinglish_roman: Human sperm cells mein lysosomal enzymes hote hain. These enzymes help break down the outer layer of the egg during fertilisation.

hinglish_roman: Mitochondria ko powerhouse of the cell kyun kehte hain?

hinglish_roman: Rough ER aur smooth ER mein kya difference hai?

hinglish_roman: Lysosome cell ke liye kaise helpful hota hai?

original_english: The cell membrane is selectively permeable, allowing some substances to pass through while blocking others.

original_english: Osmosis is the diffusion of water across a selectively permeable membrane.

original_english: Diffusion is the net movement of particles from higher to lower concentration.
hinglish_roman: Diffusion particles ka higher se lower concentration ki taraf net movement hota hai.
chapter: Cell: The Building Block of Life

original_english: The fluid-mosaic model explains that the cell membrane has a lipid bilayer with proteins embedded in it.
hinglish_roman: Fluid-mosaic model batata hai ki cell membrane mein ek lipid bilayer hota hai jismein proteins embedded hote hain.
chapter: Cell: The Building Block of Life

original_english: A potato piece placed in plain water swells because water moves into its cells.
hinglish_roman: Potato ka piece plain water mein rakhne se swell ho jaata hai. This happens because water moves into its cells by osmosis.
chapter: Cell: The Building Block of Life

original_english: A potato piece placed in salt solution shrinks because water moves out of its cells.
hinglish_roman: Potato ka piece salt solution mein rakhne se shrink ho jaata hai. Water moves out of its cells in this case.
chapter: Cell: The Building Block of Life

original_english: The cell membrane is about 7 to 10 nanometres thick.
hinglish_roman: Cell membrane bahut thin hoti hai. It is about 7 to 10 nanometres thick.

hinglish_roman: Osmosis kaise hoti hai cell membrane mein?

hinglish_roman: Diffusion aur osmosis mein kya difference hai?
chapter: Cell: The Building Block of Life

original_english: Plant cells have an additional covering outside the cell membrane called the cell wall.
hinglish_roman: Plant cells mein cell membrane ke bahar ek additional covering hoti hai jise cell wall kehte hain.
chapter: Cell: The Building Block of Life

original_english: The cell wall helps plants stay upright and maintain their shape.
hinglish_roman: Cell wall plants ko upright rehne aur apna shape maintain karne mein help karti hai.
chapter: Cell: The Building Block of Life

original_english: The cell wall is permeable, allowing water and dissolved minerals to pass through it.
hinglish_roman: Cell wall permeable hoti hai, jisse water aur dissolved minerals easily pass ho jaate hain.
chapter: Cell: The Building Block of Life

original_english: Fungi and bacteria also have a cell wall for protection and structural support.
hinglish_roman: Fungi aur bacteria mein bhi cell wall hoti hai. It provides protection and structural support to their cells.
chapter: Cell: The Building Block of Life

original_english: When a plant cell is placed in a concentrated sugar solution, its cell wall keeps the cell's shape unchanged.
hinglish_roman: Plant cell ko concentrated sugar solution mein rakhne par uska shape nahi badalta. This is because the rigid cell wall maintains its original shape.
chapter: Cell: The Building Block of Life

original_english: Why is a cell wall necessary in plants?
hinglish_roman: Cell wall plants mein kyun zaroori hai?
chapter: Cell: The Building Block of Life

hinglish_roman: Cell wall aur cell membrane mein kya fark hai?
chapter: Cell: The Building Block of Life

original_english: What is the cell wall made of?
hinglish_roman: Cell wall kis se bani hoti hai?
chapter: Cell: The Building Block of Life

original_english: A mature plant cell has one large central vacuole filled with a watery fluid called cell sap.
hinglish_roman: Mature plant cell mein ek bada central vacuole hota hai jo cell sap naam ke watery fluid se bhara hota hai.
chapter: Cell: The Building Block of Life

original_english: The vacuole stores water, minerals, sugars and waste material in the cell.
hinglish_roman: Vacuole cell mein water, minerals, sugars aur waste material store karta hai.
chapter: Cell: The Building Block of Life

original_english: Chromoplasts contain pigments other than chlorophyll, giving flowers and fruits their bright colours.
hinglish_roman: Chromoplasts mein chlorophyll ke alawa pigments hote hain, jo flowers aur fruits ko unke bright colours dete hain.
chapter: Cell: The Building Block of Life

original_english: Leucoplasts are colourless plastids that store food material like starch, oils or proteins.
hinglish_roman: Leucoplasts colourless plastids hote hain. They store food material such as starch, oils or proteins.

original_english: Why does a plant wilt when it does not get enough water?
hinglish_roman: Plant wilt kyun ho jaata hai jab usko paani nahi milta?
chapter: Cell: The Building Block of Life

hinglish_roman: Cell membrain selecteevly parmiabel hoti hai aur sirf kuch hi substancees ko pass karne deti hai.

chapter: Cell: The Building Block of Life

original_english: Life begins when a single cell divides itself several times to give rise to a large number of cells.
hinglish_roman: Life tab shuru hoti hai jab ek single cell kai baar divide hoke bahut saari cells banata hai.

original_english: These cells gradually form the skin, muscles, bones, nerves and all other organs.
hinglish_roman: Yeh cells dheere-dheere skin, muscles, bones, nerves aur baaki saare organs banate hain.

original_english: A tissue is a group of cells similar in structure that work together to perform a specific function.
hinglish_roman: Tissue aise cells ka group hota hai jo structure mein similar hote hain aur ek specific function perform karte hain.

original_english: In multicellular organisms, cells of similar type performing similar functions group together to form a tissue.
hinglish_roman: Multicellular organisms mein similar type ke cells jo similar functions perform karte hain, mil ke tissue banate hain.

original_english: The formation of different types of tissues leads to the division of labour, which increases efficiency.
hinglish_roman: Alag-alag types ke tissues banne se division of labour hoti hai, jisse body ki efficiency badh jaati hai.

original_english: Most plants are fixed in one place and do not move from place to place like animals.
hinglish_roman: Zyaadatar plants ek jagah fixed rehte hain aur animals ki tarah ek jagah se doosri jagah nahi jaate.

original_english: Plant cells have a cell wall that provides rigidity and strength.
hinglish_roman: Plant cells mein ek cell wall hoti hai jo unhe rigidity aur strength deti hai.

original_english: Without a rigid cell wall, animal cells can change shape easily, which helps in locomotion.
hinglish_roman: Rigid cell wall na hone ki wajah se animal cells aasaani se shape change kar sakti hain, jo locomotion mein help karta hai.

original_english: Meristematic tissue is made up of actively dividing cells.
hinglish_roman: Meristematic tissue actively divide hone waale cells se bana hota hai.

original_english: Roots grow only from their tips, which contain cells that divide continuously.
hinglish_roman: Roots sirf apni tips se hi grow karti hain, jahan continuously divide hone waale cells hote hain.

original_english: Apical meristem is located at the tips of roots and shoots, and helps plants grow in length.
hinglish_roman: Apical meristem roots aur shoots ki tips pe hota hai aur plants ko length mein grow karne mein help karta hai.

original_english: Lateral meristem is located along the circumference of stems and causes an increase in girth.
hinglish_roman: Lateral meristem stem ke circumference ke along hota hai aur stem ki girth badhata hai.

original_english: Annual growth rings on a tree trunk help scientists estimate the age of the tree.
hinglish_roman: Tree trunk ke annual growth rings dekh ke scientists tree ki age estimate kar sakte hain.

original_english: Intercalary meristem is located at the nodes and helps plants regenerate after being cut or grazed.
hinglish_roman: Intercalary meristem nodes pe hota hai aur plants ko cut ya graze hone ke baad regenerate karne mein help karta hai.

original_english: Grass grows back after being mowed because of the intercalary meristem present at the nodes of its stem.
hinglish_roman: Ghaas mow hone ke baad dobara ug aati hai kyunki uske stem ke nodes pe intercalary meristem hota hai.

original_english: Meristematic cells have thin walls, dense cytoplasm and a large prominent nucleus.
hinglish_roman: Meristematic cells ki walls thin hoti hain, cytoplasm dense hota hai aur nucleus bada aur prominent hota hai.

original_english: Meristematic cells lack vacuoles and are tightly packed with little intercellular space.
hinglish_roman: Meristematic cells mein vacuoles nahi hote aur yeh cells tightly packed hote hain jisme bahut kam intercellular space hoti hai.

original_english: Differentiation is the process by which meristematic tissue loses the ability to divide and becomes permanent tissue.
hinglish_roman: Differentiation woh process hai jisme meristematic tissue divide karne ki ability kho deta hai aur permanent tissue ban jaata hai.

original_english: Permanent tissues can be simple, composed of only one type of cell, or complex, composed of more than one type.
hinglish_roman: Permanent tissues simple ho sakte hain, jisme sirf ek type ki cells hoti hain, ya complex, jisme ek se zyada types ki cells hoti hain.

original_english: Epidermis forms the outermost layer of the plant body and protects all parts of the plant.
hinglish_roman: Epidermis plant body ki sabse bahari layer hoti hai aur plant ke sabhi parts ko protect karti hai.

original_english: Epidermal cells are covered with a waxy layer of cutin called cuticle, which reduces water loss.
hinglish_roman: Epidermal cells ke upar cutin ki ek waxy layer hoti hai jise cuticle kehte hain, jo water loss kam karta hai.

original_english: Root hairs increase the surface area for absorption of water and minerals from the soil.
hinglish_roman: Root hairs surface area badhate hain jisse mitti se water aur minerals absorb karna aasaan ho jaata hai.

original_english: Stomata in leaves help in gaseous exchange and also in transpiration.
hinglish_roman: Leaves mein stomata gaseous exchange mein aur transpiration mein bhi help karte hain.

original_english: Parenchyma consists of living cells with thin walls and intercellular spaces, and mainly stores food.
hinglish_roman: Parenchyma mein thin walls waale living cells hote hain jinke beech intercellular spaces hoti hain, aur yeh mainly food store karta hai.

original_english: In aquatic plants, specialised parenchyma forms air spaces that help them float.
hinglish_roman: Aquatic plants mein specialised parenchyma air spaces banata hai jisse woh plants paani mein float kar sakti hain.

original_english: Collenchyma has living cells with unevenly thickened corners due to pectin deposition.
hinglish_roman: Collenchyma mein living cells hoti hain jinke corners pectin jamne ki wajah se uneven tarike se thick ho jaate hain.

original_english: Collenchyma provides support and flexibility, allowing stems and tendrils to bend without breaking.
hinglish_roman: Collenchyma support aur flexibility deta hai, jisse stems aur tendrils bina toote jhuk sakte hain.

original_english: Sclerenchyma cells have thick walls due to lignin deposition, making them hard and strong.
hinglish_roman: Sclerenchyma cells ki walls lignin jamne ki wajah se thick hoti hain, jisse yeh cells kaafi hard aur strong hoti hain.

original_english: Sclerenchyma cells are mostly dead and are found in stems, leaf veins, and hard coverings like coconut husk.
hinglish_roman: Sclerenchyma cells zyaadatar dead hoti hain aur stems, leaf veins aur coconut husk jaise hard coverings mein milti hain.

original_english: Xylem transports water and minerals from the roots to other parts of the plant.
hinglish_roman: Xylem roots se paani aur minerals plant ke baaki hisson tak transport karta hai.

original_english: Xylem consists of tracheids, vessels, xylem parenchyma and xylem fibres.
hinglish_roman: Xylem mein tracheids, vessels, xylem parenchyma aur xylem fibres hote hain.

original_english: Xylem parenchyma is the only living component of xylem; tracheids, vessels and xylem fibres are dead.
hinglish_roman: Xylem parenchyma xylem ka ekelauta living component hai; tracheids, vessels aur xylem fibres dead hote hain.

original_english: Phloem transports food prepared in leaves to other parts of the plant.
hinglish_roman: Phloem leaves mein bana hua khaana plant ke doosre hisson tak le jaata hai.

original_english: Phloem consists of sieve tubes, companion cells, phloem parenchyma and phloem fibres.
hinglish_roman: Phloem mein sieve tubes, companion cells, phloem parenchyma aur phloem fibres hote hain.

original_english: Companion cells regulate the loading and unloading of sugars in sieve tubes.
hinglish_roman: Companion cells sieve tubes mein sugars ka loading aur unloading regulate karti hain.

original_english: Plant tissues are organised into three tissue systems: dermal, ground and vascular.
hinglish_roman: Plant tissues teen tissue systems mein organised hote hain: dermal, ground aur vascular.

original_english: The dermal tissue system forms the outer covering of the plant, protecting it and reducing water loss.
hinglish_roman: Dermal tissue system plant ki bahari covering banata hai, plant ko protect karta hai aur water loss kam karta hai.

original_english: The ground tissue system forms the main body of the plant and includes parenchyma, collenchyma and sclerenchyma.
hinglish_roman: Ground tissue system plant ka main body banata hai aur isme parenchyma, collenchyma aur sclerenchyma aate hain.

original_english: Epithelial tissue forms the outer covering of the body and lines the internal organs.
hinglish_roman: Epithelial tissue body ki bahari covering banata hai aur internal organs ko andar se line karta hai.

original_english: Epithelial tissue is composed of closely packed cells with very little space between them.
hinglish_roman: Epithelial tissue mein cells bahut closely packed hoti hain, jinke beech bahut kam space hoti hai.

original_english: Blood is a connective tissue that transports nutrients, gases and hormones throughout the body.
hinglish_roman: Blood ek connective tissue hai jo poore body mein nutrients, gases aur hormones transport karta hai.

original_english: Red blood cells contain haemoglobin, an iron-rich protein that gives blood its red colour.
hinglish_roman: Red blood cells mein haemoglobin hota hai jo ek iron-rich protein hai aur blood ko laal rang deta hai.

original_english: Platelets help in blood clotting at the site of injury.
hinglish_roman: Platelets chot ki jagah pe blood clotting mein help karte hain.

original_english: White blood cells collect at infected areas causing redness, swelling and possible pus formation.
hinglish_roman: White blood cells infected areas mein jama hote hain jisse laalipan, sujan aur kabhi-kabhi pus bhi ban jaata hai.

original_english: Bone is a hard connective tissue with a rigid matrix containing calcium and phosphorus.
hinglish_roman: Bone ek hard connective tissue hai jisme calcium aur phosphorus waala rigid matrix hota hai.

original_english: Cartilage has a soft jelly-like matrix that provides flexibility and cushions the ends of bones.
hinglish_roman: Cartilage mein soft jelly-jaisi matrix hoti hai jo flexibility deti hai aur bones ke ends ko cushion karti hai.

original_english: Tendons connect muscles to bones and transmit the force generated by muscle contraction.
hinglish_roman: Tendons muscles ko bones se connect karte hain aur muscle contraction se jo force aati hai use bone tak pahunchaate hain.

original_english: Ligaments connect bones to bones and prevent excessive movement at joints.
hinglish_roman: Ligaments bones ko bones se connect karte hain aur joints pe zyada movement rokthe hain.

original_english: Skeletal muscles are responsible for voluntary movements and are attached to the skeleton.
hinglish_roman: Skeletal muscles voluntary movements ke liye zimmedaar hote hain aur skeleton se attached hote hain.

original_english: Skeletal muscle fibres are long, cylindrical, unbranched and multinucleate with light and dark striations.
hinglish_roman: Skeletal muscle fibres lambe, cylindrical, unbranched aur multinucleate hote hain aur inme light-dark striations dikhayi deti hain.

original_english: Smooth muscles are found in organs like the stomach and intestines and control involuntary movements.
hinglish_roman: Smooth muscles stomach aur intestines jaisi jagah mein hoti hain aur involuntary movements control karti hain.

original_english: Smooth muscle cells are spindle-shaped, have a single nucleus and lack striations.
hinglish_roman: Smooth muscle cells spindle-shaped hoti hain, ek hi nucleus hota hai aur inme striations nahi hote.

original_english: Cardiac muscles are found only in the heart and work continuously without fatigue.
hinglish_roman: Cardiac muscles sirf dil mein hoti hain aur bina thake lagaataar kaam karti rehti hain.

original_english: Cardiac muscle fibres are cylindrical, branched with a single nucleus and have faint striations.
hinglish_roman: Cardiac muscle fibres cylindrical aur branched hote hain, ek nucleus hota hai aur inme halki striations hoti hain.

original_english: Nervous tissue forms the body's control and coordination network.
hinglish_roman: Nervous tissue body ke control aur coordination network ka kaam karta hai.

original_english: Neurons are the basic cells of nervous tissue, specialised to receive, process and transmit messages.
hinglish_roman: Neurons nervous tissue ki basic cells hain jo messages receive, process aur transmit karne ke liye specialised hoti hain.

original_english: Each neuron has three main parts: a cell body, dendrites and an axon.
hinglish_roman: Har neuron ke teen main parts hote hain: cell body, dendrites aur axon.

original_english: Dendrites receive signals from other neurons, while the axon carries messages away from the cell body.
hinglish_roman: Dendrites doosre neurons se signals receive karte hain, jabki axon messages cell body se door le jaata hai.

original_english: The musculoskeletal system consists of bones, muscles, joints, cartilage, tendons and ligaments.
hinglish_roman: Musculoskeletal system mein bones, muscles, joints, cartilage, tendons aur ligaments aate hain.

original_english: The adult human skeleton makes up about 12 to 15 percent of body weight.
hinglish_roman: Ek adult insaan ka skeleton body weight ka lagbhag 12 se 15 percent hota hai.

original_english: The ball and socket joint at the shoulder allows movement forward, backward, sideways and in circles.
hinglish_roman: Shoulder pe ball and socket joint hoti hai jo aage, peeche, side mein aur gol-gol movement allow karta hai.

original_english: Hinge joints, like those in the elbow and knee, allow bending in only one direction.
hinglish_roman: Hinge joints, jaise elbow aur knee mein hoti hain, sirf ek direction mein jhukne deti hain.

original_english: The pivot joint connecting the skull to the backbone allows the head to move side to side.
hinglish_roman: Khopdi aur backbone ko jodhne waala pivot joint sar ko ek taraf se doosri taraf hilane deta hai.

original_english: The bones of the skull are connected by fixed joints, which keep the brain safe.
hinglish_roman: Khopdi ki bones fixed joints se judi hoti hain, jo brain ko surakshit rakhti hain.

original_english: The vertebral column or backbone is made up of small bones called vertebrae.
hinglish_roman: Vertebral column ya backbone chote-chote bones se bana hota hai jinhe vertebrae kehte hain.

original_english: Between each vertebra is a cartilage disc that acts as a cushion and allows flexibility.
hinglish_roman: Har do vertebrae ke beech ek cartilage disc hoti hai jo cushion ki tarah kaam karti hai aur flexibility deti hai.

original_english: The rib cage consists of 12 pairs of ribs and protects vital organs like the heart and lungs.
hinglish_roman: Rib cage mein 12 jodon ki pasliyaan hoti hain jo dil aur lungs jaise vital organs ko protect karta hai.

original_english: Ribs are joined by flexible cartilage that allows the chest to expand and contract during breathing.
hinglish_roman: Pasliyaan flexible cartilage se judi hoti hain jo chest ko saas lete waqt pheelne aur sikodhne deta hai.

original_english: F.C. Steward demonstrated that even single phloem cells of carrot can regenerate a whole plant.
hinglish_roman: F.C. Steward ne dikhaya ki gajar ke phloem ki ek akeli cell bhi poora plant dobara bana sakti hai.

original_english: Totipotency is the ability of a mature cell to dedifferentiate, divide and develop into a complete new organism.
hinglish_roman: Totipotency ek mature cell ki woh ability hai jisme woh dedifferentiate hoke divide ho sakti hai aur ek poore naye organism mein develop ho sakti hai.

original_english: Agrobacterium tumefaciens causes crown gall disease, which leads to tumour-like swellings on plant stems.
hinglish_roman: Agrobacterium tumefaciens crown gall disease karta hai, jisme plant ke stems pe tumour-jaisi gaanthein bann jaati hain.

original_english: Stem cells in bone marrow are special cells that can divide and make new blood cells.
hinglish_roman: Bone marrow mein stem cells hoti hain jo special cells hain aur naye blood cells bana sakti hain.

original_english: Transpiration creates a pull in the xylem that helps water move up from roots to leaves.
hinglish_roman: Transpiration xylem mein ek pull create karta hai jo paani ko roots se leaves tak upar jaane mein help karta hai.

original_english: In unicellular organisms like amoeba, a single cell performs all functions of life.
hinglish_roman: Amoeba jaise unicellular organisms mein ek akeli cell hi zindagi ke saare kaam karti hai.

original_english: Sipra Guha Mukherjee and S.C. Maheshwari developed a complete plant through anther culture in a laboratory.
hinglish_roman: Sipra Guha Mukherjee aur S.C. Maheshwari ne laboratory mein anther culture se ek poora plant develop kiya.

original_english: Sclerenchyma cells have thick lignified walls and are mostly dead.
hinglish_roman: Sclerenchyma cells mein thin walls hoti hain aur yeh living cells hote hain.
hinglish_with_error: Sclerenchyma cells mein thin walls hoti hain aur yeh living cells hote hain.
error_word: thin walls hoti hain aur yeh living cells hote hain
correct_word: thick lignified walls hoti hain aur yeh mostly dead cells hote hain
explanation: Student ne sclerenchyma ki properties galat likhi hain. 'Thin walls' aur 'living' dono galat hain. Sclerenchyma ki walls thick aur lignified hoti hain aur yeh cells mostly dead hote hain. Yeh collenchyma ki properties se confuse ho sakti hain.

original_english: Xylem transports water and minerals from roots to other parts of the plant.
hinglish_roman: Xylem leaves se food ko roots tak transport karta hain.
hinglish_with_error: Xylem leaves se food ko roots tak transport karta hain.
explanation: 'Xylem' ek singular subject hai isliye 'karta hai' hona chahiye, 'karta hain' nahi. 'Hain' plural subjects ke saath use hota hai. Iske alawa yeh sentence factually bhi galat hai kyunki xylem food nahi balki water aur minerals transport karta hai - woh phloem ka kaam hai.

original_english: Tendons connect muscles to bones.
hinglish_roman: Tendons bones ko bones se connecting hain.
hinglish_with_error: Tendons bones ko bones se connecting hain.
explanation: Hinglish mein English present participle 'connecting' directly use karna galat hai. Sahi form hai 'connect karte hain' jisme English verb ke saath Hindi auxiliary 'karte hain' lagate hain. Yeh ek common intra-sentential mixing error hai.

original_english: Epithelial tissue forms the outer covering of the body.
hinglish_roman: Epithelial tissue body ke outer covering banata hai.
hinglish_with_error: Epithelial tissue body ke outer covering banata hai.
explanation: Hindi mein 'covering' feminine noun hai isliye 'ki' use hona chahiye, 'ke' nahi. 'Ke' masculine nouns ke saath use hota hai. Yeh ek common gender agreement mistake hai jo Hindi-English mixing mein frequently hoti hai.

original_english: Each neuron has three main parts: cell body, dendrites and axon.
hinglish_roman: Har neuron ke teen main parts hote hain: cell body, dendrites aur axons.
hinglish_with_error: Har neuron ke teen main parts hote hain: cell body, dendrites aur axons.
explanation: Ek neuron mein sirf ek axon hota hai, isliye 'axon' singular use hona chahiye. 'Axons' likh ke student ne galat pluralization ki hai. 'Dendrites' zaroor plural hai kyunki ek neuron mein multiple dendrites hote hain, lekin axon hamesha ek hi hota hai.

original_english: Life begins when a single cell divides itself several times to give rise to a large number of cells.
hinglish_roman: Life ek single cell se shuru hoti hai jo baar baar divide hoke bahut saari cells banati hai.

original_english: A tissue is a group of cells similar in structure that work together to perform a specific function.
hinglish_roman: Tissue un cells ka group hota hai jo structure mein similar hote hain aur ek specific function perform karte hain.

original_english: In multicellular organisms, cells of similar type performing similar function group together to form a tissue.
hinglish_roman: Multicellular organisms mein similar type ki cells jo similar function perform karti hain woh group hoke tissue banati hain.

original_english: In unicellular organisms like amoeba, a single cell performs all functions of life.
hinglish_roman: Amoeba jaise unicellular organisms mein ek hi cell life ke saare functions perform karti hai.

original_english: The formation of different types of tissues leads to division of labour, which increases efficiency of the body.
hinglish_roman: Alag alag tissues banne se division of labour hota hai, jisse body ki efficiency badh jaati hai.

original_english: What is a tissue and how is it formed?
hinglish_roman: Tissue kya hota hai aur yeh kaise banta hai?

original_english: Why don't unicellular organisms have tissues?
hinglish_roman: Unicellular organisms mein tissues kyun nahi hote?

original_english: How is a tissue formed from cells in multicellular organisms?
hinglish_roman: Multicellular organisms mein cells se tissue kaise banta hai?

original_english: How does division of labour happen because of tissues?
hinglish_roman: Division of labour tissues ki wajah se kaise hota hai?

original_english: Sir, why are plant and animal tissues different?
hinglish_roman: Sir, plant aur animal tissues alag kyun hote hain?

original_english: Meristematic tissue consists of actively dividing cells that help plants grow.
hinglish_roman: Meristematic tissue mein actively dividing cells hoti hain jo plant ko grow karne mein help karti hain.

original_english: Apical meristem is located at the tips of roots and shoots and helps plants grow in length.
hinglish_roman: Apical meristem root aur shoot ke tips par hota hai aur plant ko length mein grow karne mein help karta hai.

original_english: Lateral meristem is present along the circumference of the stem and increases girth.
hinglish_roman: Lateral meristem stem ke circumference ke around hota hai aur girth ko increase karta hai.

original_english: Intercalary meristem is located at the base of internodes and helps plants regenerate after cutting.
hinglish_roman: Intercalary meristem internode ke base par hota hai aur cutting ke baad plant ko regenerate hone mein help karta hai.

original_english: Cells of meristematic tissue have thin walls, dense cytoplasm and a large prominent nucleus.
hinglish_roman: Meristematic tissue ki cells mein thin walls, dense cytoplasm aur ek bada prominent nucleus hota hai.

original_english: What is the difference between apical meristem and lateral meristem?
hinglish_roman: Apical meristem aur lateral meristem mein kya difference hai?

original_english: Where is intercalary meristem found and what is its function?
hinglish_roman: Intercalary meristem kahan paya jaata hai aur iska kya kaam hai?

original_english: What is meristematic tissue and where is it found?
hinglish_roman: Meristematic tissue kya hai aur yeh kahan paya jaata hai?

original_english: Why does root growth stop when the tip is cut?
hinglish_roman: Roots ki growth stop kyun ho jaati hai jab tip cut kar diya jaata hai?

original_english: Why do meristematic cells not have vacuoles?
hinglish_roman: Meristematic cells mein vacuoles kyun nahi hote?

original_english: Meristematic tissue becomes permanent by the process of differentiation.
hinglish_roman: Differentiation ke process se meristematic tissue permanent tissue ban jaata hai.

original_english: Parenchyma consists of living cells with thin walls that are loosely packed with intercellular spaces.
hinglish_roman: Parenchyma living cells se bani hoti hai jinki walls thin hoti hain aur cells loosely packed hote hain intercellular spaces ke saath.

original_english: Parenchyma mainly stores food and also performs photosynthesis in green parts of plants.
hinglish_roman: Parenchyma mainly food store karta hai aur plants ke green parts mein photosynthesis bhi perform karta hai.

original_english: Collenchyma consists of living cells with unevenly thickened corners due to pectin deposition.
hinglish_roman: Collenchyma living cells se bana hota hai jinke corners pectin deposition ki wajah se unevenly thick ho jaate hain.

original_english: Collenchyma provides support and flexibility, allowing stems and tendrils to bend without breaking.
hinglish_roman: Collenchyma support aur flexibility deta hai, isliye stems aur tendrils bina toote bend kar sakte hain.

original_english: Sclerenchyma cells have thick walls due to deposition of lignin, making them hard and strong.
hinglish_roman: Sclerenchyma cells ki walls lignin deposition ki wajah se thick hoti hain, isliye yeh hard aur strong ho jaati hain.

original_english: Most sclerenchyma cells are dead and are found in stems, leaf veins and hard coverings of seeds.
hinglish_roman: Sclerenchyma ki zyaadatar cells dead hoti hain aur stems, leaf veins aur seeds ke hard coverings mein paayi jaati hain.

original_english: What is the difference between parenchyma, collenchyma and sclerenchyma?
hinglish_roman: Parenchyma, collenchyma aur sclerenchyma mein kya fark hai?

original_english: Why are sclerenchyma cells dead?
hinglish_roman: Sclerenchyma cells dead kyun hote hain?

original_english: How does collenchyma tissue make the stem flexible?
hinglish_roman: Collenchyma tissue stem ko flexible kaise banata hai?

original_english: What is differentiation and how does it happen?
hinglish_roman: Differentiation kya hoti hai aur yeh kaise hoti hai?

original_english: How does parenchyma perform photosynthesis?
hinglish_roman: Parenchyma photosynthesis kaise perform karta hai?

original_english: Xylem is the tissue that transports water and minerals from roots to other parts of the plant.
hinglish_roman: Xylem woh tissue hai jo roots se water aur minerals ko plant ke baaki parts tak transport karta hai.

original_english: Xylem consists of tracheids, vessels, xylem parenchyma and xylem fibres.
hinglish_roman: Xylem tracheids, vessels, xylem parenchyma aur xylem fibres se milkar bana hota hai.

original_english: Phloem is mostly made up of living cells and transports food from leaves to other parts of the plant.
hinglish_roman: Phloem mostly living cells se bana hota hai aur leaves se food ko plant ke baaki parts tak transport karta hai.

original_english: Sieve tubes transport food while companion cells regulate their function.
hinglish_roman: Sieve tubes food transport karti hain jabki companion cells unka function regulate karti hain.

original_english: The epidermis forms the outermost layer of the plant body and protects all parts of the plant.
hinglish_roman: Epidermis plant body ki outermost layer banati hai aur plant ke saare parts ko protect karti hai.

original_english: Stomata present in leaf epidermis help in gaseous exchange and transpiration.
hinglish_roman: Leaf epidermis mein present stomata gaseous exchange aur transpiration mein help karte hain.

original_english: What is the function of xylem and phloem?
hinglish_roman: Xylem aur phloem ka kya function hai?

original_english: What is the relation between sieve tubes and companion cells?
hinglish_roman: Sieve tubes aur companion cells mein kya relation hai?

original_english: What is the function of stomata?
hinglish_roman: Stomata ka kya kaam hota hai?

original_english: How does the epidermis protect the plant?
hinglish_roman: Epidermis plant ko kaise protect karti hai?

original_english: Epithelial tissue forms the outer covering of the body and also lines internal organs like the mouth and intestine.
hinglish_roman: Epithelial tissue body ki outer covering banata hai aur mouth aur intestine jaise internal organs ko bhi line karta hai.

original_english: Epithelial tissue is composed of closely packed cells with very little space between them.
hinglish_roman: Epithelial tissue closely packed cells se bana hota hai jinke beech mein bahut kam space hota hai.

original_english: A single layer of thin, flat cells helps in rapid diffusion of gases in the lungs.
hinglish_roman: Ek single layer of thin, flat cells lungs mein gases ke rapid diffusion mein help karti hai.

original_english: Many layers of tightly packed flat cells protect the skin and mouth from mechanical injury.
hinglish_roman: Many layers ki tightly packed flat cells skin aur mouth ko mechanical injury se protect karti hain.

original_english: Cells specialised for secretion produce mucus, enzymes, hormones and sweat.
hinglish_roman: Secretion ke liye specialised cells mucus, enzymes, hormones aur sweat produce karti hain.

original_english: Ciliated epithelial cells in the nostrils and inner ear perform sensory functions like smell and balance.
hinglish_roman: Nostrils aur inner ear mein ciliated epithelial cells smell aur balance jaisi sensory functions perform karti hain.

original_english: Columnar epithelial cells in the small intestine help in efficient absorption of nutrients.
hinglish_roman: Small intestine mein columnar epithelial cells nutrients ke efficient absorption mein help karti hain.

original_english: What is the main function of epithelial tissue?
hinglish_roman: Epithelial tissue ka main function kya hota hai?

original_english: Why is epithelial tissue in the lungs only a single layer?
hinglish_roman: Lungs mein epithelial tissue single layer ki kyun hoti hai?

original_english: What is the difference between squamous, columnar and cuboidal epithelium?
hinglish_roman: Squamous, columnar aur cuboidal epithelium mein kya difference hai?

original_english: Where are ciliated cells found and what is their function?
hinglish_roman: Ciliated cells kahan paayi jaati hain aur inka kya function hai?

original_english: How many layers of epithelial tissue are there in the skin?
hinglish_roman: Skin mein epithelial tissue kitni layers ki hoti hai?

original_english: A tissue that connects and supports other tissues is called connective tissue.
hinglish_roman: Jo tissue doosre tissues ko connect aur support karta hai use connective tissue kehte hain.

original_english: Blood is a connective tissue with a watery, fluid matrix, while bone has a hard, solid matrix.
hinglish_roman: Blood ek connective tissue hai jiska matrix watery aur fluid hota hai, jabki bone ka matrix hard aur solid hota hai.

original_english: Red blood cells contain haemoglobin, an iron-rich protein, and live for about four months.
hinglish_roman: Red blood cells mein haemoglobin hota hai, jo ek iron-rich protein hai, aur yeh cells lagbhag char mahine tak zinda rehti hain.

original_english: Platelets help in blood clotting at the site of an injury.
hinglish_roman: Platelets injury ki site par blood clotting mein help karte hain.

original_english: Cartilage has a soft, jelly-like matrix and provides flexibility and cushioning to joints.
hinglish_roman: Cartilage ka matrix soft aur jelly-like hota hai aur yeh joints ko flexibility aur cushioning deta hai.

original_english: Tendons connect muscles to bones, while ligaments connect bones to bones.
hinglish_roman: Tendons muscles ko bones se connect karte hain, jabki ligaments bones ko bones se connect karte hain.

original_english: Ligaments limit movement at a joint and help prevent dislocation.
hinglish_roman: Ligaments joint par movement ko limit karte hain aur dislocation ko prevent karne mein help karte hain.

original_english: Both blood and bone are connective tissue, so how are they different?
hinglish_roman: Blood aur bone dono connective tissue hai toh yeh alag kaise hain?

original_english: What is the function of platelets?
hinglish_roman: Platelets ka function kya hai?

original_english: What is the difference between a tendon and a ligament?
hinglish_roman: Tendon aur ligament mein kya fark hai?

original_english: How does cartilage give us flexibility?
hinglish_roman: Cartilage humein flexibility kaise deta hai?

original_english: What do white blood cells do during an infection?
hinglish_roman: White blood cells infection ke time kya karte hain?

original_english: Voluntary movements like running and writing are carried out by skeletal muscles attached to the skeleton.
hinglish_roman: Running aur writing jaisi voluntary movements skeleton se attached skeletal muscles ke through hoti hain.

original_english: Skeletal muscle fibres are unbranched, multinucleate and show light and dark bands called striations.
hinglish_roman: Skeletal muscle fibres unbranched, multinucleate hoti hain aur inmein light aur dark bands hoti hain jinhe striations kehte hain.

original_english: Smooth muscles found in the stomach and intestines help in slow, continuous movements like digestion.
hinglish_roman: Stomach aur intestines mein paayi jaane wali smooth muscles digestion jaisi slow, continuous movements mein help karti hain.

original_english: Smooth muscle cells are spindle-shaped, have a single nucleus and lack striations.
hinglish_roman: Smooth muscle cells spindle-shaped hoti hain, inmein single nucleus hota hai aur striations nahi hoti.

original_english: Cardiac muscles are found only in the heart and work tirelessly throughout life without fatigue.
hinglish_roman: Cardiac muscles sirf heart mein paayi jaati hain aur yeh poori zindagi bina thake tirelessly kaam karti hain.

original_english: Cardiac muscle fibres are cylindrical and branched with a single nucleus and faint striations.
hinglish_roman: Cardiac muscle fibres cylindrical aur branched hoti hain, inmein single nucleus aur faint striations hoti hain.

original_english: What is the difference between striated and smooth muscle?
hinglish_roman: Striated aur smooth muscle mein kya difference hota hai?

original_english: Why is cardiac muscle special?
hinglish_roman: Cardiac muscle special kyun hoti hai?

original_english: What is the difference between voluntary and involuntary movements?
hinglish_roman: Voluntary aur involuntary movements mein kya fark hai?

original_english: Where is smooth muscle found and what is its function?
hinglish_roman: Smooth muscle kahan paayi jaati hai aur iska kya function hai?

original_english: Why do skeletal muscles have striations?
hinglish_roman: Skeletal muscle mein striations kyun hote hain?

original_english: Which muscle works during digestion?
hinglish_roman: Digestion ke time kaunsi muscle kaam karti hai?

original_english: Nervous tissue forms the body's control and coordination network.
hinglish_roman: Nervous tissue body ke control aur coordination ka network banata hai.

original_english: Neurons are the cells of nervous tissue that receive, process and transmit messages.
hinglish_roman: Neurons nervous tissue ki cells hoti hain jo messages ko receive, process aur transmit karti hain.

original_english: Each neuron has a cell body, dendrites and an axon.
hinglish_roman: Har neuron mein ek cell body, dendrites aur ek axon hota hai.

original_english: The cell body contains the nucleus and controls the activities of the cell.
hinglish_roman: Cell body mein nucleus hota hai jo cell ki activities ko control karta hai.

original_english: Dendrites receive signals from other neurons and pass them to the cell body.
hinglish_roman: Dendrites doosre neurons se signals receive karte hain aur unhe cell body tak pahunchate hain.

original_english: The axon is a long fibre that carries messages from the cell to the axon terminals.
hinglish_roman: Axon ek long fibre hota hai jo messages ko cell se axon terminals tak carry karta hai.

original_english: During exercise, the brain signals the heart to beat faster to meet the body's increased oxygen demand.
hinglish_roman: Exercise ke time brain heart ko signal deta hai ki woh fast beat kare taaki body ki badhi hui oxygen demand puri ho sake.

original_english: What are the main parts of a neuron?
hinglish_roman: Neuron ke main parts kya hain?

original_english: What is the functional difference between dendrites and axon?
hinglish_roman: Dendrites aur axon mein kya kaam ka fark hai?

original_english: How does the brain signal the heart to beat faster?
hinglish_roman: Brain heart ko fast beat karne ka signal kaise deta hai?

original_english: How does nervous tissue coordinate the body?
hinglish_roman: Nervous tissue body ko coordinate kaise karta hai?

original_english: What is the function of axon terminals?
hinglish_roman: Axon terminals ka kya function hota hai?

original_english: Reproduction is a biological process by which living beings produce new individuals of their own kind.
hinglish_roman: Reproduction ek biological process hai jiske zariye living beings apni hi tarah ke naye individuals paida karte hain.

original_english: Every organism has a definite life span - it is born, grows, matures, reproduces and eventually dies.
hinglish_roman: Har organism ki ek definite life span hoti hai - woh janam leta hai, badhta hai, mature hota hai, reproduce karta hai aur aakhir mein mar jaata hai.

original_english: Living beings reproduce in two main ways - asexually, where a single parent produces offspring that are almost exact copies of the parent, and sexually, where offspring inherit a mix of characteristics from the two individuals.
hinglish_roman: Living beings do tareekon se reproduce karte hain - asexually, jahan ek single parent aisa offspring produce karta hai jo almost parent ki exact copy hota hai, aur sexually, jahan offspring ko dono individuals ki mixed characteristics milti hain.

original_english: Asexual mode of reproduction is seen in many unicellular organisms like bacteria, amoeba, yeast and simple multicellular organisms like hydra and sponge.
hinglish_roman: Asexual reproduction bahut saare unicellular organisms mein dekha jaata hai jaise bacteria, amoeba, yeast aur simple multicellular organisms jaise hydra aur sponge mein.

original_english: Vegetative propagation means that new plants arise from the vegetative parts, that is, from the growing parts of a plant.
hinglish_roman: Vegetative propagation ka matlab hai ki naye plants, plant ke vegetative parts yaani growing parts se nikalte hain.

original_english: Potato and ginger have fleshy underground stems that sprout new plants without producing seeds.
hinglish_roman: Aalu aur adrak ke fleshy underground stems hote hain jo bina seeds produce kiye naye plants uga dete hain.

original_english: Bryophyllum leaves sprout tiny plantlets which eventually grow into new plants.
hinglish_roman: Bryophyllum ke patte chote-chote plantlets ugaate hain jo aakhirkar naye plants ban jaate hain.

original_english: Grafting involves inserting a stem cutting of one plant into a slit made on the rooted plant of another variety.
hinglish_roman: Grafting mein ek plant ki stem cutting ko doosri variety ke rooted plant ke slit mein fit kiya jaata hai.

original_english: In layering, a flexible twig is buried under the soil and after roots develop, it is cut from the parent plant to grow independently.
hinglish_roman: Layering mein ek flexible twig ko mitti ke neeche dabaaya jaata hai aur roots develop hone ke baad, use parent plant se kaat diya jaata hai taaki woh alag grow kar sake.

original_english: Tissue culture technique has revolutionised farming practices like banana farming by providing mass-produced healthy plantlets.
hinglish_roman: Tissue culture technique ne banana farming jaisi farming practices mein revolution la diya hai kyunki isme mass-produced healthy plantlets milte hain.

original_english: In organisms like hydra, repeated cell division at a specific site on the parent body produces a small outgrowth called a bud.
hinglish_roman: Hydra jaise organisms mein, parent body ke ek specific jagah par baar baar cell division hone se ek chhoti si outgrowth banti hai jise bud kehte hain.

original_english: The bud enlarges and separates from the parent to live independently - this process is called budding.
hinglish_roman: Bud bada hota hai aur parent se alag hokar independently jeena shuru karta hai - is process ko budding kehte hain.

original_english: Spores are lightweight, usually single-celled structures that float easily through air currents and germinate quickly into a new individual when moisture and nutrients are available.
hinglish_roman: Spores halke aur aksar single-celled hote hain jo aasaani se hawa ke saath ud jaate hain aur jab naami aur nutrients milein toh jaldi se naye individual mein germinate ho jaate hain.

original_english: In asexual reproduction, the central process is mitosis, a type of cell division that produces two daughter cells each having the same number of chromosomes as the parent cell.
hinglish_roman: Asexual reproduction mein central process mitosis hai, yeh ek aisa cell division hai jisme do daughter cells banti hain jinmein parent cell jitne hi chromosomes hote hain.

original_english: Offspring produced by asexual reproduction are genetically identical to the parent and are called clones.
hinglish_roman: Asexual reproduction se paida hone waale offspring parent ke genetically identical hote hain aur inhe clones kaha jaata hai.

original_english: Sexual reproduction involves two parents in the formation of a new individual, meaning both parents contribute to the genetic material of the offspring.
hinglish_roman: Sexual reproduction mein do parents milkar ek naya individual banate hain, yaani dono parents offspring ke genetic material mein contribute karte hain.

original_english: Meiosis is a special type of cell division that reduces the chromosome number of a parent cell from diploid to haploid in daughter cells.
hinglish_roman: Meiosis ek special type ka cell division hai jisme parent cell ke chromosomes ki sankhya diploid se haploid ho jaati hai daughter cells mein.

original_english: Humans have 23 pairs of chromosomes, which means a total of 46 chromosomes in each body cell.
hinglish_roman: Insaanon mein 23 pairs of chromosomes hote hain, matlab har body cell mein kul 46 chromosomes hote hain.

original_english: In plants, the pollen grain contains male gametes and delivers them to an ovule which contains the female gamete or egg.
hinglish_roman: Plants mein, pollen grain mein male gametes hote hain jo inhe ovule tak pohonchate hain jahan female gamete yaani egg hota hai.

original_english: Flowers serve as reproductive organs in angiosperms, which are the most diverse group of plants on Earth.
hinglish_roman: Angiosperms mein flowers reproductive organs ki tarah kaam karte hain, aur angiosperms dharti par plants ka sabse diverse group hai.

original_english: A complete flower has four parts - sepals, petals, stamens and pistil.
hinglish_roman: Ek complete flower mein chaar parts hote hain - sepals, petals, stamens aur pistil.

original_english: The stamen is the male part of a flower and consists of a filament and an anther which produces pollen grains containing male gametes.
hinglish_roman: Stamen phool ka male part hota hai aur isme ek filament aur ek anther hota hai jo male gametes wale pollen grains produce karta hai.

original_english: The pistil is the female part of the flower and has three subparts - stigma, style and ovary.
hinglish_roman: Pistil phool ka female part hota hai aur iske teen subparts hote hain - stigma, style aur ovary.

original_english: The stigma is located at the tip of the pistil and may be flat and/or sticky to receive pollen.
hinglish_roman: Stigma pistil ki tip par hota hai aur yeh flat aur/ya sticky ho sakta hai taaki pollen ko pakad sake.

original_english: The transfer of pollen grains from the anther to the stigma of a flower is called pollination.
hinglish_roman: Anther se pollen grains ka stigma tak transfer hona pollination kehlata hai.

original_english: Self-pollination is when pollen transfers to the stigma of the same flower or another flower of the same plant.
hinglish_roman: Self-pollination tab hoti hai jab pollen usi phool ke ya usi plant ke doosre phool ke stigma par transfer hota hai.

original_english: Cross-pollination happens when pollen is transferred from a flower of one plant to the stigma of a flower of another plant of the same type.
hinglish_roman: Cross-pollination tab hoti hai jab pollen ek plant ke phool se doosre same type ke plant ke phool ke stigma par jaata hai.

original_english: Pollination by wind is seen in plants like wheat, maize and rice, where pollen grains are light and small and produced in large numbers.
hinglish_roman: Wheat, maize aur rice jaise plants mein wind se pollination hoti hai, jahan pollen grains halke aur chote hote hain aur badi matra mein produce hote hain.

original_english: Insect-pollinated flowers like sunflower and hibiscus are often brightly coloured, produce nectar and give off fragrance to attract pollinators.
hinglish_roman: Sunflower aur hibiscus jaise insect-pollinated flowers aksar chamkeelay rang ke hote hain, nectar produce karte hain aur pollinators ko attract karne ke liye khushbu dete hain.

original_english: Once pollen reaches a compatible stigma, pollen grains produce pollen tubes that grow down through the style into the ovary.
hinglish_roman: Jab pollen compatible stigma tak pahunch jaata hai, pollen grains pollen tubes banate hain jo style ke zariye ovary mein neeche ki taraf badhti hain.

original_english: The male gamete moves through the pollen tube and arrives at the ovule where it fuses with the egg cell - this fusion is called fertilisation.
hinglish_roman: Male gamete pollen tube se hokar ovule tak pahunchta hai jahan woh egg cell se fuse hota hai - is fusion ko fertilisation kehte hain.

original_english: The fertilised egg is called a zygote, which later develops into an embryo, while the ovary develops into a fruit and ovules develop into seeds.
